add-to-a-date.quickAnswer: Adding time to a date is simple calendar arithmetic: move forward from the start date by the chosen number of days, weeks, months or years. For example, 30 days after 1 January 2026 is 31 January 2026, a Saturday. Month additions keep the same day number where possible - 1 month after 31 January lands on 3 March, because February is shorter than January.
keyFacts: Adding days is exact: the calendar moves forward one day at a time, so 30 days after 1 January 2026 is 31 January 2026.
Adding months keeps the same day number when the target month has that day. Adding 1 month to 31 January rolls into early March, because February never has 31 days.
Adding years keeps the same month and day. Adding 1 year to 29 February 2024 gives 28 February 2025, because 2025 is not a leap year.
Weeks are exact groups of 7 days, so adding weeks never changes the weekday: 3 weeks after a Monday is always a Monday.
Leap years are handled automatically, including the century rule: 2000 was a leap year, but 1900 was not.
howTo: Pick your start date using the date picker.
Enter how much time you want to add, as a whole number.
Choose the unit: days, weeks, months or years.
Read the resulting date, its weekday and its ISO (YYYY-MM-DD) form instantly.
Use the days-from-today figure to see how far in the future the result lies.
add-to-a-date.formula:
Result = start date + N units.
Days: result = start date + N days.
Weeks: result = start date + (N x 7) days.
Months: result month = start month + N (day kept when valid).
Years: result year = start year + N (same month and day).
Example: 2026-01-01 + 30 days = 2026-01-31.
add-to-a-date.workedExample:
Start date: 18 October 2026 (a Sunday).
1. Amount = 45, unit = days.
2. October has 31 days, so 18 October + 13 days = 31 October. 32 days remain: November takes 30, leaving 2 days into December.
3. Result: 2 December 2026.
4. Weekday check: 45 days = 6 full weeks + 3 days, so Sunday + 3 days = Wednesday.
ISO form: 2026-12-02.

limitations: Month arithmetic follows standard calendar rollover. Contracts sometimes define a 'month' differently - check your agreement.
Public holidays and business days are not considered; this is pure calendar math.
Time zones are ignored - the output is a calendar date, not a timestamp.
Extremely large additions (tens of thousands of years) can exceed calendar support.

faqs.q: What happens when I add 1 month to 31 January?
faqs.a: You land in early March - 3 March, or 2 March in a leap year. Date arithmetic rolls the extra days forward because February has no 31st. This matches how spreadsheets and most calendars behave.

faqs.q: Does adding weeks ever change the weekday?
faqs.a: Never. A week is exactly 7 days, so the weekday stays identical: 6 weeks after a Wednesday is always a Wednesday.
Automatically. Adding 1 year to 29 February 2024 gives 28 February 2025, and adding 4 years gives 29 February 2028.

faqs.q: Can I add a negative amount here?
faqs.a: This tool only moves forward in time. To go backwards, use the Subtract From a Date tool.

faqs.q: Does my time zone change the result?
faqs.a: No. The calculator works with plain calendar dates, so the answer is identical wherever you are.

faqs.q: What is the ISO date in the results?
faqs.a: The international YYYY-MM-DD format, for example 2026-12-02. It removes all confusion between day-first and month-first date styles.
